feedback: D1 is a clean, honest catalogue but it stops at nine findings and two of the canonical ten are absent, so it cannot earn near-full marks. You correctly classed SQL injection (A03/CWE-89), unsalted MD5 (A02/CWE-916), JWT alg:none (A07/CWE-347), the hardcoded sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 secret (A02/CWE-798), missing token expiry (A07/CWE-613), cookie flags, open redirect, and XXE, and your decoy work is the strongest part of the submission: you named the HS256 hash_equals branch, proved it constant-time, and correctly redirected blame to alg:none and the plaintext secret. What hurt you is that stored XSS to the 185.220.101.9:8443 beacon at 02:18:47 appears only in D2, not in your D1 table, and path traversal at 02:24:02 (files/?path=/etc/passwd returning root:x:0:0:) is missing entirely, so two real findings lose their share. Most of your evidence is paraphrased ('Raw concatenation in login query') rather than a quoted source line, and only Finding 1 carries a verbatim payload and timestamp, which is why the findings-1-to-5 row landed at partial. In D2 the chain is in correct order and reconciled to capture lines, and your PoC strings (the SQLi tautology, the fetch cookie beacon, the XXE entity) are verbatim and good. The CVSS work is where you lost the most: you scored SQL injection 10.0 with S:C, but the auth bypass does not change scope or hit availability, so the defensible vector is AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:H/A:N at roughly 9.1, and most of your vectors carry a string but no justifying sentence, which caps that row at partial. Your business impact is genuinely strong: 312 customers, the ₦6,400 to ₦950,000 range, the ~₦202,000 average, the tens-of-millions order-of-magnitude flagged as an estimate, and the BoltCash six-week horizon all trace to the exfil sample, so no fabrication. D3 is your best deliverable: the remediation table is ordered by risk-reduction-per-hour with effort columns rather than by raw CVSS, you correctly name SQL injection as the earliest break with JWT as an independent path, and both detection stopgaps name an exact field (the login.php username tautology pattern and the legacy_admin_jwt alg:none header) with an honest false-positive discussion including the O'Brien edge case. Two slips: you call the app a 2019 Django tool when the source is PHP (login.php), and the disproved decoy is not restated in the report itself. D4 answers all four prompts in your own voice and cites ISC2 Canon I and II by number tied to real actions, but you reference the NDPA 2023 duties without the load-bearing section numbers, and you needed section 40 (notify the NDPC within 72 hours) and section 41 (notify the 312 data subjects on high risk) named explicitly. The single most important fix: complete your catalogue and quote the actual evidence line for every finding, because a nine-of-ten table with paraphrased evidence is what separated this from a high-70s into low-80s report.
